div.div:
How it holds together
OpenBao never starts sealed for long: each pod unwraps its root key from floci (the local stand-in for a cloud KMS), so the bootstrap Job only initialises it once, writes the recovery key, seeds KV, creates the eso-reader / db-configurator / oidc-configurator roles and revokes the root token. External Secrets logs in with Kubernetes auth and re-reads KV every hour; the ten database runtime passwords come from the database engine instead (one vault_rotator per cluster) and are re-read every 15 s, because OpenBao rotates them; pods read them from a mounted file. cert-manager's homelab-ca also issues the database server and pooler certificates, and each database client namespace gets a *-db-ca-trust Certificate whose ca.crt it verifies against (verify-full). Since OpenBao 2.7 the awskms seal is an external KMS plugin, downloaded once and cached on the Raft PVC. Every request and response is written as one audit JSON line on stdout (active node only, secret values HMAC-ed), which Vector ships to VictoriaLogs and ClickHouse; vmagent scrapes /v1/sys/metrics.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1333px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1355px; margin-left: 12px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #475569;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#475569, #9ba7b8); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Planned, not deployed
TLS on the OpenBao listener, a real cloud KMS instead of floci, AppRole for CI/CD, per-request dynamic database credentials and the rest of internal TLS on homelab-ca (RFC-0020: gRPC, Temporal, Keycloak, S3, Valkey). Locally the edge certificate is issued by homelab-ca; Let's Encrypt DNS-01 with the Cloudflare token is the production path.
